title: B₂[r] Sum Sets vs Difference Sets
description: For B₂[r] sets in {1,...,N}, do the asymptotic constants cᵣ (sums) and c'ᵣ (differences) differ when r ≥ 2? For r = 1 (Sidon sets), c₁ = c'₁ = 1. Erdős conjectured c'ᵣ < cᵣ. Open.

meta.author: Erdős, Berend, Freud
meta.assumptions: None. 0 axioms, 0 sorries. All 13 theorems proved from Lean primitives. The open conjecture (cᵣ ≠ c'ᵣ for r ≥ 2) is described in comments — not stated as an axiom or theorem.

overview.historicalContext: Sidon sets (B₂[1] sets) are among the most studied objects in additive combinatorics: a set A where all pairwise sums a+b (a ≤ b) are distinct. The classical result that the maximum Sidon set in {1,...,N} has size ~√N dates to Erdős and Turán (1941), with the upper bound sharpened by Lindström (1969) and the lower bound achieved by Singer's difference set construction (1938). B₂[r] sets generalize this by allowing each integer to have at most r representations as a sum a+b. Erdős posed Problem 863 in conversation with Berend, and independently with Freud, around 1992 [Er92c]. The key question is whether the symmetry between sums and differences, which holds perfectly for r=1, breaks for r ≥ 2. Erdős conjectured that for r ≥ 2, the difference constant c'ᵣ is strictly less than the sum constant cᵣ. The intuition is that the ordered nature of sums (a+b with a ≤ b) and the unordered nature of differences (a-b for any a,b) create fundamentally different counting behaviors when multiple representations are allowed. Cilleruelo, Ruzsa, and Trujillo (2002) established |A| ≤ (rN)^{1/2} + O(r^{1/2}N^{1/4}) for B₂[r] sets, showing the growth rate is Θ(√(rN)). Ruzsa showed c_r ≤ √r with constructions giving c_r ≥ √r - o(1), but analogous precision for c'_r has not been achieved. Even the existence of the limiting constants cᵣ and c'ᵣ is nontrivial for r ≥ 2.
overview.problemStatement: For r ≥ 2, are the maximal sizes of B₂[r] sets (sums) and difference B₂[r] sets in {1,...,N} asymptotically different? Specifically, is c'ᵣ < cᵣ?
overview.text: For B₂[r] sets in {1,...,N}, do the asymptotic constants cᵣ (sums) and c'ᵣ (differences) differ when r ≥ 2? For r = 1 (Sidon sets), c₁ = c'₁ = 1. Erdős conjectured c'ᵣ < cᵣ. Open.
overview.proofStrategy: Defines sum and difference representation counts, B₂[r] and difference B₂[r] properties, and their maximum sizes maxB2rSize/maxDiffB2rSize in {1,...,N}, then proves the infrastructure lemmas: monotonicity in r and N, empty/singleton base cases, the crude |A|² representation bounds, subset heredity, and the B₂[1] ↔ Sidon equivalence. The classical r=1 equality and both forms of the open conjecture (c'ᵣ < cᵣ, and the weaker cᵣ ≠ c'ᵣ) are documented in comments only — no asymptotic constant, √N growth rate, or ε-δ/Filter.atTop convergence is formalized.
keyInsights: **Classical Equality at r=1:** For Sidon sets, both sum and difference B₂[1] sets achieve maximum size ~√N, giving c₁ = c'₁ = 1. The upper bound (Lindström 1969) and lower bound (Singer 1938) match for both versions.

**Structural Asymmetry:** Sum representations count pairs (a,b) with a ≤ b and a+b = n, while difference representations count pairs with a-b = n. The ordering constraint in sums versus the sign freedom in differences creates fundamentally different combinatorial structures when r ≥ 2.

**Direction of Inequality:** Erdős specifically conjectured c'ᵣ < cᵣ (not just c'ᵣ ≠ cᵣ), predicting that difference-restricted sets are smaller. The weaker form just asks for inequality in either direction.

**Growth Rate:** Cilleruelo-Ruzsa-Trujillo (2002) established that B₂[r] sets in {1,...,N} have size Θ(√(rN)), with Ruzsa showing c_r ~ √r, but the precision needed to separate c_r from c'_r has not been achieved.

**Formalized scope:** What is machine-checked here is the definitional layer and its structural lemmas — monotonicity, subset heredity, empty/singleton base cases, the crude |A|² representation bounds, and the B₂[1] ↔ Sidon equivalence. The extremal quantities maxB2rSize/maxDiffB2rSize are defined, but the asymptotic constants cᵣ, c'ᵣ, their √N growth, and any ε-δ/Filter.atTop convergence are not formalized; the conjecture itself remains open and lives only in comments.

sections.title: Problem Statement and Imports
sections.summary: Module documentation describing Problem 863 and its context, with imports for Data.Nat.Basic, Data.Finset.Basic, Data.Finset.Card, Order.Filter.Basic (for eventually/atTop), and Tactic.

sections.title: B₂[r] Set Definitions
sections.summary: Four core definitions: sumRepCount (ordered sum pairs a ≤ b with a+b = n), IsB2r (at most r sum representations), diffRepCount (difference pairs a-b = n over Z), and IsDiffB2r (at most r nonzero difference representations).

sections.title: Containment Predicate
sections.summary: Defines InRange A N asserting A ⊆ {1,...,N}, restricting to the standard finite interval for Sidon-type extremal problems.

sections.title: Maximum Set Sizes
sections.summary: Defines maxB2rSize and maxDiffB2rSize as maxima over powerset of {0,...,N} filtered by the B₂[r] and InRange conditions, using Finset.sup with Finset.card as the objective.

sections.title: Classical Sidon Case (r = 1)
sections.summary: Comment stating the classical r=1 baseline: both the sum and difference B₂[1] (Sidon) extremal sizes grow as ~√N with equal constants c₁ = c'₁ = 1. Documented as background; not formalized as a theorem (the asymptotic is classical).

sections.title: The Erdős Problem (Main and Weak Conjectures)
sections.summary: Comment section stating Erdős Problem 863. Main conjecture: for r ≥ 2 the asymptotic constants cᵣ (sums) and c'ᵣ (differences) satisfy c'ᵣ < cᵣ, so difference sets are strictly smaller. Weak conjecture: there exists r ≥ 2 with cᵣ ≠ c'ᵣ. Both are open and documented as background, not formalized as theorems or axioms.

sections.title: Part II: Basic Properties of B₂[r] Sets
sections.summary: Ten proved theorems: monotonicity of IsB2r and IsDiffB2r in r (isB2r_mono, isDiffB2r_mono), monotonicity of InRange in N (inRange_mono), empty-set lemmas (inRange_empty, isB2r_empty, isDiffB2r_empty), crude cardinality bounds sumRepCount/diffRepCount ≤ |A|² (sumRepCount_le_card_sq, diffRepCount_le_card_sq), and downward closure under subsets (isB2r_subset, isDiffB2r_subset).

sections.title: Connection to Sidon Sets (Erdős #340)
sections.summary: Links the r=1 case to Sidon sets. Defines IsSidonSetLocal (all ordered sums a+b with a ≤ b are distinct, matching IsSidonSet from Erdos340Problem.lean) and proves the equivalence isB2r_one_iff_sidon: a set is B₂[1] iff it is Sidon. Also proves singleton sets are both B₂[r] and difference B₂[r] for r ≥ 1 (isB2r_singleton, isDiffB2r_singleton).

mainTheorems.name: isB2r_one_iff_sidon
mainTheorems.significance: The conceptual heart of the file: a B₂[1] set is exactly a Sidon set (all ordered sums a+b, a ≤ b, distinct). Anchors the r = 1 case c₁ = c'₁ = 1 and connects Erdős #863 to the Sidon-set formalisation of Erdős #340.
mainTheorems.description: Both directions from Finset.card_le_one: unique representation ⇔ each sum-fibre has ≤ 1 element. Forward exhibits the two witnessing pairs in the same singleton filter; backward reads distinctness off the ≤1 cardinality.

mainTheorems.name: isB2r_mono
mainTheorems.statement: IsB2r A r → r ≤ r' → IsB2r A r'
mainTheorems.significance: The B₂[r] constraint is monotone in the multiplicity bound r: a set with at most r sum-representations trivially has at most r' ≥ r. Underlies the nesting B₂[1] ⊆ B₂[2] ⊆ … of the whole hierarchy.
mainTheorems.description: Pointwise le_trans (h n) hrr on the per-value representation counts.

mainTheorems.name: isDiffB2r_mono
mainTheorems.statement: IsDiffB2r A r → r ≤ r' → IsDiffB2r A r'
mainTheorems.significance: Difference analogue of isB2r_mono: the difference-B₂[r] property is monotone in r. Keeps the sum and difference hierarchies structurally parallel — the symmetry Erdős's conjecture probes.
mainTheorems.description: Pointwise le_trans (h n hn) hrr, quantified over nonzero differences n.

mainTheorems.name: isB2r_subset
mainTheorems.statement: IsB2r A r → A' ⊆ A → IsB2r A' r
mainTheorems.significance: The B₂[r] property is hereditary under subsets, so maximal-size B₂[r] sets are well posed and every B₂[r] set sits inside one. Essential for the maxB2rSize supremum to behave.
mainTheorems.description: calc: sumRepCount A' n ≤ sumRepCount A n (filter of a product-subset) ≤ r, via Finset.card_le_card and product_subset_product.

mainTheorems.name: isDiffB2r_subset
mainTheorems.statement: IsDiffB2r A r → A' ⊆ A → IsDiffB2r A' r
mainTheorems.significance: Difference-set analogue of isB2r_subset: heredity under subsets for difference B₂[r] sets, making maxDiffB2rSize equally well posed.
mainTheorems.description: Same calc as the sum case applied to diffRepCount over nonzero differences.

mainTheorems.name: sumRepCount_le_card_sq
mainTheorems.significance: A crude but foundational bound: no value has more than |A|² sum-representations, since the representations are a filtered subset of A × A. The trivial ceiling every B₂[r] refinement improves on.

mainTheorems.name: diffRepCount_le_card_sq
mainTheorems.significance: Difference analogue of sumRepCount_le_card_sq: at most |A|² difference-representations of any integer.

mainTheorems.name: isB2r_singleton
mainTheorems.significance: Base case witnessing that B₂[r] sets are nonempty: any singleton is B₂[r] for r ≥ 1, so the extremal quantities range over a nontrivial family.
mainTheorems.description: sumRepCount {a} n ≤ card({a}×{a}) = 1 ≤ r via card_filter_le and product_singleton_singleton.

mainTheorems.name: isDiffB2r_singleton
mainTheorems.significance: Difference analogue: any singleton is a difference B₂[r] set for r ≥ 1.
mainTheorems.description: diffRepCount {a} n ≤ 1 ≤ r by the same singleton-product argument.

mainTheorems.name: isB2r_empty
mainTheorems.significance: The empty set is B₂[r] for every r — the vacuous base of the hierarchy (every value has 0 ≤ r representations).
mainTheorems.description: simp [sumRepCount]: the empty product filters to the empty set.

mainTheorems.name: isDiffB2r_empty
mainTheorems.significance: The empty set is a difference B₂[r] set for every r.

mainTheorems.name: inRange_mono
mainTheorems.statement: InRange A N → N ≤ N' → InRange A N'
mainTheorems.significance: Containment A ⊆ {1,…,N} is monotone in the window N, so enlarging the ambient interval preserves admissibility — needed to compare maxB2rSize across N when taking asymptotics.
mainTheorems.description: Pointwise: keeps the lower bound 1 ≤ a and relaxes a ≤ N to a ≤ N' by le_trans.

mainTheorems.name: inRange_empty
mainTheorems.significance: The empty set lies in every window {1,…,N}; together with isB2r_empty it certifies the admissible family filtered by maxB2rSize is never empty.

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem 863 asks whether B₂[r] sets and difference B₂[r] sets have different asymptotic constants for r ≥ 2. The classical Sidon case (r=1) has equal constants c₁ = c'₁ = 1, but the generalization is wide open. The formalization provides all definitions and the proved structural infrastructure (monotonicity, heredity, base cases, |A|² bounds, B₂[1] ↔ Sidon); the classical baseline and both the strong and weak forms of the conjecture are documented in comments, not formalized as theorems or axioms.
conclusion.implications: Resolution would reveal whether additive and subtractive combinatorial structures diverge beyond the Sidon threshold, with implications for the theory of additive bases, representation functions, and the fine structure of B_h sets. The problem connects to questions about additive energy, the Erdős-Turán conjecture on additive bases, and the theory of perfect difference sets.
openQuestions: Do the limits cᵣ and c'ᵣ exist for all r ≥ 2? Even proving convergence of the ratios is nontrivial.
Is c'ᵣ < cᵣ or c'ᵣ > cᵣ for r = 2? This is the smallest open case.
What are the exact values of c₂ and c'₂? Current bounds are not precise enough to distinguish them.
How do the constants cᵣ and c'ᵣ grow as r → ∞? Is c_r/c'_r bounded or unbounded?
Can computational evidence for small r (e.g., r = 2, 3) and moderate N distinguish cᵣ from c'ᵣ?

crossReferences.description: Erdős #949 studies sum-free sets and continuum-sized sumset avoidance, sharing the theme of additive structure in sets with restricted representation counts.
Erdős #795 investigates multiplicative Sidon sets (distinct subset products), the multiplicative analogue of the B₂[1] property central to this problem.
Erdős #530 studies maximum Sidon subsets of finite sets, directly related to the B₂[1] baseline case where c₁ = c'₁ = 1.
